title: {y} and {en} - There and Some
description: Say there and some without repeating the place or the thing.
can_do: Say how many you have with {j'en ai deux}.
line: Use {y} for a place and {en} for some, so you don't repeat what was just said.

parts.heading: {y}: there
text: {y} stands for a place you already named, usually after {à}, {au}, {dans} or {chez}. It goes before the verb, where {le} and {la} go.

lines: Tu vas au café ? Oui, j'y vais.
Are you going to the café? Yes, I'm going there.
Vous allez chez Paul ? Oui, nous y allons.
Are you going to Paul's? Yes, we're going there.
Le chat est dans la maison ? Oui, il y est.
Is the cat in the house? Yes, it's in there.

parts.heading: {en}: some, of them
text: {en} stands for something you already named after {de}, {du}, {de la} or {des}, or with a number. It goes before the verb too.
parts.note: With a number, the number goes at the end: {j'en ai deux}. English can drop “of them”, but French keeps {en}.

lines: Tu veux du café ? Oui, j'en veux.
Do you want some coffee? Yes, I want some.
Tu as des chats ? Oui, j'en ai deux.
Do you have cats? Yes, I have two.
Tu as besoin d'aide ? Oui, j'en ai besoin.
Do you need help? Yes, I need some.

parts.heading: With {ne … pas}
text: {ne} goes before {y} or {en}, and {pas} goes after the verb.

lines: Non, je n'y vais pas.
No, I'm not going there.
Non, je n'en veux pas.
No, I don't want any.

parts.heading: In commands and set phrases
text: In a positive command, {y} and {en} go after the verb with a hyphen, like {le} in {donne-le}. A few phrases you already know are built this way.

lines: Vas-y !
Go ahead!
Allons-y !
Let's go!
On y va ?
Shall we go?
Prends-en !
Take some!

checks.ask: Which one means “Yes, I'm going there”?
checks.why: {y} stands for the place and goes before the verb: {j'y vais}.

checks.ask: {Tu veux du café ?} Which answer means “Yes, I want some”?
checks.why: {en} stands for {du café} and goes before the verb: {j'en veux}.

checks.ask: {Tu as des chiens ?} Which answer means “Yes, I have two”?
checks.why: With a number, {en} still goes before the verb, and the number comes at the end: {j'en ai deux}.
